articleTitle: Developing Cuboid Recognition-based AR Application for Preschool Marine Education
abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) is widely used in education because of its ability to deepen learning interactions by overlaying virtual objects with the real world. However, there is a lack of empirical studies on the impact of using AR in preschool marine education. To address this issue, this paper developed a cuboid recognition-based AR application and applied it to preschool marine courses, and further investigated its impact on students’ learning achievement and motivation. We adopted a quasi-experimental approach, using a pretest and posttest to measure learning achievement and scales to measure motivation and technology acceptance. A total of 60 students in the middle grades of kindergarten were randomly assigned to an experimental group and a control group. Students in the experimental group learned about the knowledge using the iPad AR application, while students in the control group learned the same material using traditional teaching methods. The results showed that the students in the experimental group scored higher than the students in the control group in terms of learning achievement and motivation (attention, confidence, relevance, and satisfaction). In addition, students in the experimental group had a high level of technology acceptance for teaching with the AR application. Our study provides an empirical basis for the application of AR in preschool marine education. In addition, this paper illustrates how the cuboid recognition-based AR application can be developed for formal educational purposes.

articleTitle: The Effects of AR-Based Virtual Teacher Environment on Preschooler’s Language Learning
abstract: With the increasing application of technologies, Augmented Reality (AR) is increasingly being used in educational fields to facilitate the student’s learning experience. However, relatively few studies on AR combined with virtual teacher environments to facilitate preschool children’s language learning. Therefore, this study designed a mobile AR application that embeds a virtual teacher, which assists the children in learning English vocabulary. This study used a quasi-experimental method, using a pre-test and post-test to measure learning achievement, and scales to measure children’s presence and foreign language classroom anxiety. 40 kindergarten students from two classes were randomly divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group used an AR app, while the control group learned in a traditional classroom. Results showed that compared with the control group, the children who used the AR application integrated with the virtual teacher had a stronger sense of presence, lower foreign language classroom anxiety, and higher learning achievement. The results provide a new type of learning practice case for AR-based language learning in preschool education.

articleTitle: Relation between academic anxiety and primary school students’ academic achievement: problem-solving ability as mediator
abstract: This study explored the relationships among academic anxiety, academic achievement and problem-solving ability. Participants were 683 students from 10 primary schools in Wuhan, China. We analyzed participants’ scores including academic anxiety, problem solving ability, and the latest examination scores. Structural equation model and bias-corrected bootstrap method were used in this study. The results showed that academic anxiety not only affected academic achievement directly and negatively, but also indirectly affected academic achievement through problem solving ability. Therefore, it was suggested to alleviate students’ academic anxiety by creating a good learning environment, focus on the development of problem-solving ability, improve students’ academic achievement. This study contributed to understanding the important role of problem-solving ability in academic anxiety and academic achievement, provided a reference for how to improve academic achievement.

articleTitle: The effects of creative thinking on students’ cognitive learning outcomes: A literature review
abstract: This study discovered a positive relationship between students’ creative thinking and cognitive learning outcomes after analyzing 20 peer-reviewed journal articles. It also emphasized that creative thinking has the potential to transform problem-solving techniques and lead to improved academic performance. However, more research is needed to investigate the relationship between students’ creative thinking and affective and behavioral learning outcomes. The study highlights the importance of developing creative thinking skills in students in order to improve their cognitive learning outcomes.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on Human-Machine Collaborative MOOC Learning Interaction Empowered by Generative AI
abstract: Human-machine collaboration is the future trend of the human social learning. The new data generation capability of the Generative AI has been proven on similar pre-trained models such as ChatGPT. MOOC is an important engine to drive the digital transformation of the higher education in the world. The innovative and practical researches of the human-machine collaborative MOOC learning interaction can offer useful references to build the digital learning ecology with high quality. Guided by the interaction theory and the curriculum theory, this study sorted out the general process of the human-machine collaborative MOOC learning. Then, based on the Human in the Loop (HITL), this study deconstructed the mechanism of the human-machine collaborative MOOC learning interaction, and clarified the empowerment function of the Generative AI. After that, the pattern of the human-machine collaborative MOOC learning interaction empowered by the Generative AI, which constituted with “self-content-society”, was constructed, and it was applied through a national open online course with high quality from the iCourse. Finally, the results of the quantity and quality analysis of the social interactions in the MOOC discussion forum showed that the interaction patterns mentioned above could effectively improve learners’ interactive validity and learning quality.

articleTitle: Application of the Tablet-based AR in Preschooler’s Science Education
abstract: With the increasing growing interest in emerging technologies in education, augmented reality (AR) is used in diversified educational fields to support students’ learning. However, there are few studies on the application of AR in preschool children’s science education. This study aimed at exploring the effect of tablet-based AR application on preschool children’s science learning achievement, interaction level, and immersion in the process of science learning in the context of the classroom setting. The study used a quasi-experimental approach, using a pretest and posttest to measure learning achievement, a scale to measure children’s immersion, and observation cards to measure children’s interaction levels. The 40 kindergarten students from two classes were randomly divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group used tablet-based AR app to learn science lessons, and the control group learned the same material through traditional teaching methods. The results showed that students who used tablet-based AR app had significantly higher science learning performance compared to students who learned through traditional methods. In addition, children who used AR app in the classroom had a high level of interaction, and their level of classroom interaction had a strong correlation with academic performance.

articleTitle: The Impact of stem Courses on Students’ Computational Thinking: Mediation based on problem solving ability and stem attitude
abstract: Computational thinking is advocated as a skill that everyone should possess, and stem content and background can be conducive to the learning of computational thinking. This study constructed a theoretical model of the impact of stem courses on students’ computational thinking, and measured the mediating effects of problem solving skills and stem attitudes on stem courses and students’ computational thinking. The study included a questionnaire of 1870 secondary school students and a descriptive, correlational and mediating analysis. The results show that stem courses can predict students’ computational thinking through students’ problem solving ability and students’ attitude towards stem. The results of this study have a positive reference value for discussing the factors affecting students’ computational thinking, implementing stem course education, improving students’ problem-solving ability and enhancing students’ attitude towards stem.

articleTitle: Research on the design and application of early childhood language education activities supported by information technology
abstract: As a key component of early childhood education, language teaching is an effective way to cultivate children’s oral expression abilities. The teaching process supported by information technology is more vivid and intuitive, which is in line with the characteristics of preschool children. Kindergarten teachers should combine information technology with language teaching and fully leverage its advantages. This study selected 40 children from a senior kindergarten class as research subjects and divided them into two groups: a traditional teaching group and a technology-supported teaching group, to explore the impact of language education activities supported by information technology on children’s language learning. The teaching process was observed, recorded, and analyzed. The results showed that the performance of children in the technology-supported group was significantly better than that in the traditional teaching group in terms of “initiative,” “goal awareness,” “imagination and creativity,” “curiosity,” and “concentration.” Children’s language expression and communication abilities were improved, and sentence expressiveness was also better.

articleTitle: Development of the Youth Digital Citizenship Assessment Scale: Analysis Based on CTT, IRT and GT
abstract: The improvement of teenagers’ digital citizenship is one of the most significant tasks, which can not only make progress on their literacy, but also promote their all-round development. The development of scale is the key to accurately evaluate digital citizenship. However, there is no appropriate scale to evaluate teenagers’ digital citizenship for China. This study explores the biggest conflict on digital citizenship evaluation in the current academic community, which is whether to conduct total factor evaluation or only examine key elements. At the same time, it also explains that the current digital citizenship evaluation tools and methods may have serious errors due to the limitations of scale evaluation and Classical Test Theory (CTT). It provides a reference for future research, so that accurate evaluation of the whole process and all factors of digital citizenship can be achieved. This study expands the theory and method of digital citizenship evaluation, and builds a high accuracy digital citizenship scale, which provides an effective reference for accurately evaluating teenagers’ digital citizenship and fostering digital citizens.

articleTitle: Blended Teaching Reform and Assessment of Petrochemical Technology
abstract: In view of the problems existing in the course teaching, blended teaching reform was used in the Petrochemical Technology with six-step teaching method, which based on “problem-oriented” and “quality expansion project” with the help of information technology such as “rain class” and “MOOC”. During the teaching process, “students’ feedback” was paid attention to. The content and process of “teaching” and “learning” were reconstructed according to the refinery enterprises technology. The “quality dextension project” were focused on before and after class. The teaching activities was paid attention to the process before, during and after the class, so the students’ classroom participation was improved to 100%. At the same time, the online evaluation system of curriculum was innovated. During the two teaching cycles, the percentage of excellent students increased from 32% to 70%.

articleTitle: Action Research on Scientific Inquiry Activity Empowered by Virtual Simulation in Elementary School
abstract: Cultivating innovative talents is a great plan for the long-term development of the country and the nationality. Scientific inquiry activity in elementary school is an important path to cultivate student’s awareness and competence of innovation. It is of great theoretical value and significance to explore the empowerment of virtual simulation on scientific inquiry activity in elementary school and to improve students’ scientific literacy. This study is guided by theories such as inquiry-based teaching, applied methods of literature research and action research, proposed the general process of scientific inquiry activity in elementary school, and clarified the empowerment of virtual simulation on scientific inquiry activity. After two rounds of action research, this study carried out the teaching practice and summarized a process model of scientific inquiry activity empowered by virtual simulation. Finally, applying an assessment indicator to evaluate and analyze the effect of scientific inquiry activity empowered by virtual simulation, the results proved that this kind of activity could effectively increase scientific inquiry knowledge, improve scientific inquiry competence, and stimulate interest in scientific inquiry.

articleTitle: A Corpus-aided Study of Thinking Quality in English Language Textbooks in China
abstract: The rapidly changing knowledge society has become more demanding in terms of the thinking quality of citizens, and the education system must ensure new literacies in new competencies, as well as new ways of learning. Starting from thinking quality, one of the core literacies of English subjects required by the English Curriculum Standard of General Senior High Schools (2017 Edition, 2020 Revision), this paper attempts to analyze the embodiment and characteristics of the development of thinking quality in the latest English textbooks for senior high school (2019 edition), and focus on teaching activities pointing to the development of thinking quality using the corpus search tool #Lancsbox. The results show a high frequency and richness of vocabulary reflecting thinking quality and a high number of teaching activities targeting the development of thinking quality. This study explores how to use corpus analysis to evaluate the development of thinking quality in the latest English textbooks for senior high school, and provides implications for corpus-assisted textbook analysis and senior high school English teaching, with a view to providing reference for teachers who are currently using new textbooks to cultivate students’ thinking quality.

articleTitle: Research on the Design and Practice of Mathematics Flipped Classroom under ICT Environment in Middle School
abstract: Mathematics flipped classroom under ICT environment refers to a classroom form in which students experience meaningful “before-in-after-class” mathematics learning, complete a series of challenging mathematics learning tasks, and acquire mathematics deep learning ability based on teachers’ professional learning design and intelligent technology application. This study adopts rfcs/gn-based research methods, puts forward a mathematics flipped classroom teaching model under ICT environment based on deep learning and learning design theory and carries out mathematics flipped classroom teaching experiments in middle school. The results show that the model can improve students’ mathematics performance, and make students’ deep learning abilities develop.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on the Influencing Factors of K-12 students’ Online Learning Intention
abstract: Online learning intention is critical for K-12 students to remain engaged in online learning. This study employed structural equation modeling to investigate the potential factors that influence K-12 students’ online learning intention. A total of 831 valid questionnaires were collected from K-12 students in China participated in the survey. The findings reveal that: (1) perceived value has an exceptional impact on online learning intention, outweighing all other factors. (2) perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness of technology in online learning had a minor effect on students’ learning experiences and their online learning intention. This indicates that technology-related challenges are no longer insurmountable for online learning. (3) learning motivation has a positive indirect influence on online learning intention through perceived value. (4) teaching activities indirectly boost online learning intentions through Perceived Value. (5) teacher feedback has not been effectively utilized in online learning.

articleTitle: Identification of personalised learning needs: A literature review
abstract: This paper reports on a review study concerning research related to the identification of the personalised learning needs of learners. It addresses the various learning needs examined in related studies, the types of technique used, and the types of data collected to identify the learning needs. A total of 348 publications on personalised learning between 2011 and 2021 were collected from Scopus for analysis. The findings show various personalised learning needs identified in the literature, with the most common being learning experiences, learning resources, and tutoring. These needs were often identified through the types of technique used, such as learning platform, learner assessment, and learner profile. The most frequently collected data was learning performance and learning behaviours. The findings reveal the patterns in the approaches and technologies used for identifying the learning needs of individual learners. This being the first step in providing personalised support to address their needs.

articleTitle: Concept and Possible Impacts of a Study Planning Assistant in Higher Education
abstract: While digital study assistants (DSA) have been subject to a rising scholarly interest, the university system landscapes which they are to be integrated into are often decentralized and historically grown. In this paper, we introduce a concept of a DSA against the background of the exemplary system landscape of the University of Bamberg, Germany. We outline such a system’s functionality based on a prototypical implementation, touching upon related research and discussing possible broader impact in higher education. We also address the challenges that are faced when integrating a DSA into a university context.

articleTitle: Motivating Medical Students’ Active Learning Supported By Constructing An Autonomous Learning Environment
abstract: The speed and mode of knowledge growth have broken the previous ways of information acquisition and transmission, and we have entered an era of lifelong education and lifelong learning. School education is also undergoing drastic changes, and How to stimulate students’ learning initiative and improve their active learning ability have become critical issues. Active learning involves multiple development processes such as cognition, behavior, emotion, and interaction with the environment. It requires creating a learning environment suitable for students’ active learning and the necessary supporting conditions with the help of information technology under the influence of the outside world and culture. Based on medical computed tomography (CT) imaging diagnosis course, this paper elaborates and analyses the current learning environment and gives some countermeasures and suggestions on effectively motivating students’ active learning based on information technology. This paper proposes to construct a mobile and individualized active learning environment with multi-interaction of teacher-student interaction, student-student interaction, and human-computer interaction from six aspects: sharing of resources, visualization of content, intellectualization of assessment, virtualization of operation, individualized recommendation, online communication and mobility of learning place, to effectively stimulate students’ active learning and promote the development of active learning activities.

articleTitle: Learning Gaps in Project-based Requirements Engineering Education - A Case Study of Student Projects
abstract: [Context and motivation] Learning Requirements Engineering is one of the key activities in teaching Software Engineering. Training computer science students to appreciate the importance of requirement engineering in practice is essential but also a difficult task. [Question/problem] In software requirements engineering education courses, project-based practice is commonly adopted as the pedagogical approach. However, feedback shows that projects taken in the class resulted in poorly translated requirements engineering skill sets required in the industry. [Principal ideas/results] This paper is to investigate and illustrate the student learning gaps observed in project-based requirements engineering education. Data containing software requirements were collected from 72 Computer Science student projects. The grounded theory approach had been systematically adopted, and keywords classified by requirements engineering activities were extracted from assessment comments. Based on the analysis of the comment keywords and report details, the issues exposed in student projects have been observed and summarized. Integrating with existing requirements engineering research, we discuss the causes from the teachers’ perspective. The leading causes of students’ underperformance in requirements engineering education learning outcomes are the lack of the industry environment, the lack of domain knowledge, and the lack of problem-solving skills. [Contribution] This paper contributes to the current educational effort in preparing students for the requirements engineering and software engineering community.

articleTitle: Validating Plagiarism Detection Systems with Metamorphic Testing
abstract: Context: Plagiarism is a severe issue in the academic world, and plagiarism detection systems are commonly used to find plagiarism violations. Although advanced technologies have improved plagiarism detection systems, there is a lack of focus on assessing their effectiveness and performance. Objective: Plagiarism detection systems give a local optimum rather than a global optimum, which leads to a test oracle problem. Therefore, a feasible and novel approach to validate those systems is required. Method: We propose Metamorphic Testing (MT) to validate plagiarism detection systems. Metamorphic relations (MRs) validate the relations between inputs and outputs, which are vital components of MT. Based on the concept of Metamorphic relations patterns (MRP), three MRs are proposed to generate follow-up test inputs while characteristics of the source test outputs are preserved. If the proposed MRs are violated, faults in the system will be detected. Results: The experimental results show that the proposed MRs can validate four plagiarism detection systems. Conclusion: The result shows that MT can systematically and effectively validate plagiarism detection systems. Subsequent studies can further extend MT applications in validating other plagiarism detection systems by applying proposed MRs or exploring other MRs related to the semantics of source text corpus.

articleTitle: Integrating Student Response System into English as a Foreign Language Classroom: A Preliminary Study
abstract: This study discusses the use of Student Response Systems (SRS) in the context of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning, exploring how SRS affects learners’ EFL anxiety and enjoyment. The study investigates whether the use of an SRS can increase EFL learners’ enjoyment and reduce their anxiety. A quasi-experimental design was used, with 58 undergraduate students from a Chinese university participating in the study. Their EFL anxiety and enjoyment were measured using validated questionnaires both before and after the intervention. Results showed that the treatment group outperformed their counterparts in the control group in terms of EFL anxiety with a small-to-medium effect size. Additionally, the use of SRS significantly reduced EFL anxiety in the treatment group over the six-week-long intervention with a small-to-medium effect size. However, regarding enjoyment, there was no significant difference between the two groups, and the treatment group did not have a significant increase in enjoyment. This preliminary study suggests that SRS can be an effective tool for reducing negative emotions in relation to EFL learning.

Index Terms: Results Of The Independent Samples T-test

articleTitle: Exploring the Characteristics of Online Learning Behavior in Blended Learning
abstract: Blended learning is a learning style that combines a portion of learning materials and learning activities through an online learning platform. By studying the characteristics of online learning behaviors of freshmen in blended learning, we can further help them to better carry out their undergraduate study life. Through the study of online learning behavior characteristics of freshmen participating in blended learning, this article finds that: (1) Learners with siblings are more engaged in online learning behaviors than those without siblings, and the difference in forum participation is most significant. (2) Using K-means clustering analysis, learners can be classified into four categories based on their online learning characteristics learners: Comprehensive learners, Performance-oriented learners, Social learners and Task-oriented learners. (3) Learners with higher level of engagement in online learning are more likely to achieve better grades.

articleTitle: Trending or Obsolete? A Systematic Review of Facebook-Supported Learning in Higher Education from 2013 to 2022
abstract: This research conducted a systematic literature review on the application of Facebook in higher education published between 2013 and 2022 with the aim of examining the extent to which studies use Facebook as an educational tool in higher education. After an initial literature search and manual screening, a total of 34 articles from the Web of Science Core Collection were identified. The literature analysis used a coding scheme that included six interrelated aspects: metadata, research, technological features, instructional design, implementation, and assessment. The results of the review revealed the trend patterns in Facebook-supported higher education in terms of publication, technological features, instructional designs, and the characteristic of implementation and assessment. Finally, several implications for promoting Facebook-supported higher education are proposed.

articleTitle: Research on Teaching Strategies to Promote Classroom Interaction in Smart Classroom Environment
abstract: Classroom interaction is one of the important factors that affect students’ learning effects, and curriculum reform is constantly updating the requirements for classroom interaction. At the same time, existing studies have shown that in a typical smart learning environment, smart classrooms play an auxiliary role in classroom interaction. Therefore, many scholars study classroom interaction in a smart classroom environment from the perspective of technology usage and human-technology interaction. Based on the smart classroom environment, this study proposes three teaching strategies to promote classroom interaction: classroom resource preparation strategies, technology-supported cooperative learning strategies, and technology-based evaluation and feedback strategies, and conducts quasi-experimental research. The results of the video analysis show that The implementation of the teaching plan based on teaching strategies has had a positive impact on teacher-student interaction and human-computer interaction. These conclusions provide practical teaching guidance and reference for the specific implementation of the new curriculum standards.

articleTitle: Research on the application strategy of chemistry teaching based on digital science argument mapping
abstract: In 2022, a new version of the Compulsory Education Chemistry Curriculum Standards was released, and its core literacy shift places more emphasis on the cultivation and development of higher-order competencies, yet how to effectively promote the development of chemistry subject competencies in the learning process is a challenge that has been constantly explored. With the continuous development of information technology in education, various tools dedicated to help learners learn have been introduced and have played an important role in the transformation of education. In this paper, we take the perspective of digital scientific argumentation diagrams and build a preliminary application model for chemistry teaching and learning, and its role in the development of chemistry subject competence. The paper also aims to promote the educational use of digital scientific argumentation diagrams.

articleTitle: A study on the effect of topic design on peer interaction behavior and cognitive level in online course forums
abstract: Peer interaction is the key to promoting learners’ knowledge construction and enhancing learning effectiveness, which is conducive to developing students’ higher-order thinking. Meaningful topics can stimulate students’ interest in learning. Currently, teacher questioning and topic design are mostly mentioned as part of course instruction, and research on questioning to guide student interaction in online courses is still shallow, mostly staying at the theoretical level and proposing strategies. In view of this, the present study classifies and designs the types of topics in online forums, and explores the temporal variation of learners’ discussions and the impact of different types of topics on the level of interactive behavior and cognitive level based on the Social Epistemic Network Signature (SENS) Analysis method. The study showed that Socratic topics as tasks were more likely to attract learners’ attention and response to the topics than factual and problem-solving topics; core learners’ prestige status in the network was less affected with increasing k-core in the social network, but node activity decreased; Socratic topics in epistemic networks could enhance learners’ cognitive level of depth and breadth, and promote the formation of higher-order thinking.

articleTitle: Computational Thinking and Academic Achievement: The Mediator Roles of Problem-solving Ability and Learning Anxiety
abstract: Computational thinking (CT) has received increasing attention from educational researchers as a higher-order thinking skill. CT is a key factor that influences the learning process and facilitates the acquisition of knowledge and the improvement of students’ academic performance. However, the mechanisms of how CT affects students’ academic performance have yet to be explored in depth. Based on this, this study used a large-scale questionnaire to construct a model with problem-solving ability and learning anxiety as mediators with 8,134 Chinese elementary school students. The results showed that CT was a significant direct predictor of academic achievement; problem-solving ability and learning anxiety played significant mediator roles between CT and students’ academic achievement. CT can improve students’ problem-solving ability and reduce anxiety, which leads to better academic performance.

articleTitle: Construction of Adaptive Learning Framework in the Online Learning Environment
abstract: An online learning environment means a new education system based on Internet technology and thinking. This environment has greatly changed traditional education. Based on this background, this study takes adaptive learning for online education as the theme, and under the correct guidance of the full-perspective learning theory, constructs an adaptive personalized learning framework of four dimensions and two processes, and expounds the improvement of adaptive learning for learners in all dimensions, Relying on the guidance of intelligent technology, excavate the relationship between technologies, comprehensively analyze the necessity of building adaptive learning framework in the online education, build adaptive learning framework in online learning environment, accurately diagnose the main problems existing in learners’ learning process, timely carry out teaching intervention and guidance, meet learners’ personalized learning needs, and commit to promoting higher quality education resources and personalized services for learners, Constantly meet the diverse needs of learners such as fragmented learning, ubiquitous learning, and lifelong learning. Therefore, this study investigates and analyzes the main problems in online learning, and makes a preliminary analysis of the relevant articles on adaptive learning. The purpose is to realize the construction of adaptive learning framework and the establishment of an indicator evaluation system through a series of technical empowerment and serve the construction of a learning society.

articleTitle: Design of Serious Games for Blended Learning: Virtual Reality or Augmented Reality?
abstract: Blended learning has become a popular teaching and learning approach, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, because it integrates different learning modalities, such as face-to-face instruction, online learning, and self-paced study, to create a more engaging and effective learning experience for students. One of these learning modalities is serious games, which gamify the learning experience to further enhance students’ engagement and improve their learning outcomes. Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) are two technologies that can be used to create serious games for blended learning. Deciding which technology to use in the design of a serious game can be challenging. This paper provides an overview of the current trends of using VR and AR on serious games for blended learning purposes and examines the considerations to be taken into account in designing such a serious game, which are expected to be useful to practitioners adopting VR/AR and gamification in blended learning environments.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of Students’ Engagement in Blended Synchronous Learning
abstract: Student engagement is identified as the key predictor of students’ academic performance. However, few studies have explored the factors that influence students’ engagement in blended synchronous learning (BSL). Based on the Triadic Reciprocal Determinism Theory, this study explores the factors affecting students’ engagement from the individual factors (academic self-efficacy and motivation), environmental factor (social presence), and behavioral factors (teacher-student interaction and student-student interaction). The results show that academic self-efficacy, motivation, and social presence are observed to be the predictors of the three specific types of engagement in BSL. Teacher-student interaction is observed to be the predictor of behavioral engagement and emotional engagement, while student-student interaction predicts emotional engagement. These findings can provide references for optimizing the instructional design to improve students’ engagement in BSL.

articleTitle: Teaching on Needs: A Study on the Characteristics of Adult Online Learning
abstract: With the popularization of lifelong learning, online learning has increasingly become the main way for adult learners to acquire knowledge and skills. In order to analyze the influencing factors and their influencing mechanism on adult online deep learning, and explore online teaching strategies to effectively promote the occurrence of deep learning, this study developed the Occurrence Mechanism Model of Adult Online Deep Learning based on the three stages of “Course Design-Teaching Practice-Teaching Evaluation”, and developed an online deep learning assessment tool for adults. 494 adult online learners were investigated by questionnaire. Statistical analysis and path analysis indicate that firstly, organizing teaching in real situations based on learners’ needs is the key factor to improve learning motivation and learning engagement. The design of adult online course should adhere to the idea of “Teaching on Needs”. Secondly, teachers should pay attention to the “Support-Adjustment” service for learners to promote them to develop advanced abilities such as ability for knowledge construction, communication and cooperation skills, and problem-solving skills. Finally, adult online teaching should enhance learners’ online presence and guide learners to “learning-to-learn” and “actively participate in learning”.

articleTitle: Effects of concept mapping-based review strategy on students’ literature review writing ability and critical thinking tendency
abstract: Literature review writing ability is an important part of scientific research ability. It is always a challenging goal to improve students’ literature review writing ability in higher education Research Methods course. In this study, a concept mapping-based review strategy was developed to improve the literature review writing ability and critical thinking tendency of undergraduates. Two groups of pre-test and post-test experiments were conducted on Educational Research Methods course in a university. The results display that: Concept maps can significantly improve students’ critical thinking tendency; Concept maps can indirectly promote students’ literature review writing ability. Students with higher critical thinking tendency have higher literature review writing ability; Moreover, Concept maps can promote students’ comprehension of literature review moves.

articleTitle: Research on Primary School English Teaching Model Against Language Attrition in Blended Learning Environment
abstract: English plays an increasingly important role in international communication and technological development. Therefore, the learning of English has gradually become the focus at primary school education in China. However, due to the immaturity of primary school students’ language development system, English language attrition has become a huge dilemma faced by primary school English teaching in China. Blended learning environments provide students with richer learning resources, more independent learning and more personalized learning methods, which has great advantages in promoting the acquisition, understanding and application of language knowledge. Therefore, this study proposed a T-RADIO model based on information technology to resist language attrition, and then designed experiments according to relevant influencing factors for practical verification. Finally, it was found that the digital schema intervention can help solve the problem of language attrition in primary school English learning. And the T-RADIO theoretical framework can minimize the occurrence of language attrition and improve the efficiency of primary school students’ English learning.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on the Effectiveness of Multimodal Input and Digital Multimodal Composing on Vocabulary Learning
abstract: Among new teaching methods and activities, multimodal input (MI) and digital multimodal composing (DMC) are the popular ones. However, with numerous studies examining the effectiveness of MI, the effectiveness of DMC on vocabulary remains to be studied. Therefore, the present study aims to investigate the effects of MI and DMC on L2 vocabulary learning, and explore learners’ perceptions towards DMC. Totally 63 non-English majors participated and were divided into MI group and DMC group. They all took a proficiency test and a vocabulary pretest. The MI group learned the target words with the help of multimodal materials provided by the researchers, while the DMC group learned by creating materials. After six sessions of experiment, they took a post-test and a delayed post-test. Participants in the DMC group also completed a questionnaire and some of them were interviewed. Results showed that the DMC group performed better in terms of vocabulary acquisition and retention, and generally had a positive attitude and were motivated by DMC. However, application of technology and time consumption are the main obstacles that make participants have negative perceptions. Implications and suggestions for teaching practice and future research are provided.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Online Peer Assessment on Critical Thinking in Student Teachers: Insights from an Epistemic Network Analysis
abstract: Peer has increasingly become one of the important teaching evaluation tools in higher education in China, and a large number of existing studies have shown that peer-assessment not only promotes learners’ deeper understanding of knowledge to enhance learning effectiveness, but also enhances students’ critical thinking. Therefore, exploring the cyclical characteristics of critical thinking and the change process of internal dimensions is still an important research topic at present. In this study, with the help of an online learning platform, Xiaoya, we collected text data of comments from 67 students in online discussions, analyzed the time-series characteristics of students’ critical thinking in an eight-week course based on a critical thinking coding framework, and used epistemic network analysis (ENA) to compare different genders, main posts and replies’ epistemic network characteristics. It was found that (1) students showed positive critical thinking trends in the discussions; (2) male student teachers’ epistemic abilities were at the middle to upper level; (3) the discussions in the main post covered a wide range of topics and established connections between Applicating solutions and Recognizing problems, while some critical thinking dimensions in the replies were missing. Furthermore, by analyzing the stages of students’ critical thinking, this study provides teachers and learning designers with suggestions for students to conduct peer assessment in order to help students better understand the learning content.

articleTitle: A Study of Effective Strategies to Improve Classroom-Based Blended Learning Experience of University Students
abstract: Classroom-based blended learning is becoming a new form of higher education teaching in the post-pandemic era. Improving the classroom-based blended learning experience of university students has important theoretical significance and practical value for cultivating innovative talents who can adapt to the development of digital society. Guided by the Blended Learning Theory and the Humanistic Learning Theory, this study used literature research, theoretical deduction, and action research to clarify the connotation and elements of the university students’ classroom-based blended learning experience. Meanwhile, the effective strategies for improving the classroom-based blended learning experience of university students were initially constructed. Then, after two rounds of action research teaching practice and continuous iterative improvement, the researchers built the strategies application model to improve the classroom-based blended learning experience of university students. Finally, the evaluation scale of university students’ classroom-based blended learning experience was used to test the effect of the improvement strategies. The effect analysis showed that the improvement strategies effectively improved the classroom-based blended learning experience and the classroom-based blended learning performance of university students.

articleTitle: Supporting Engineering Education with Augmented Reality: A Systematic Review from 2000 to 2022
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) has been widely used to support teaching and learning in various disciplinary domains. One discipline merits our special attention is engineering education due to the increasing demand of quality engineers in the Information Age. This study provides a systematic review of the literature on AR-supported higher engineering education that were published between 2000 and 2022. After an initial literature search and manual screening, a total of 45 articles were selected as the study sample for this systematic review. Each article was analyzed through five related aspects of AR-supported instruction: basic information, instructional context, technology features, instructional design, and research results. The study results revealed the characteristics of AR-supported engineering education over the past 23 years in terms of publishing trends, research types, applied disciplines, instructional design, technical features, and research design. Finally, the implications and suggestions for the application of AR in engineering education are put forward.

articleTitle: A Study of Problem-solving Ability in Science and Technology Innovation Courses Under the IPO Framework: Digital Literacy as A Mediator
abstract: Science and technology innovation education is an important aspect of youth quality education. Promoting students’ problem-solving and innovation abilities through science and technology innovation activities has become an important issue that educators need to face nowadays. Based on the input-process-outcome (IPO) framework, this paper constructed a hypothetical model of the influence mechanism of students’ problem-solving ability. And we analyzed based on 1,092 survey data from a region in Wuhan, China, to verify the validity of the model. As a result of the analysis, it was found that the science and technology innovation courses (STIC) needed to be further strengthened. STIC had a significant impact on students’ problem-solving ability; digital literacy as a process variable played a mediating role between the STIC and problem-solving ability, which significantly improved students’ problem-solving ability.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Interactive Chinese Language Learning Environment for Preschool Children in Ethnic Minority Areas of Western China
abstract: China is a country with diverse ethnic groups, and the Chinese language serves as a common language among these groups. However, there are significant challenges in preschool Chinese education in ethnic minority areas of western China, including the lack of immersive, experiential, and interactive teaching environments. Therefore, this research aims to establish an intelligent interactive language learning environment for teachers and children in western ethnic minority regions, and designs four types of intelligent interactive language teaching activities. To evaluate the classroom effectiveness of this system, a quasi-experimental study was conducted with a total of 90 children, with an average age of 5.3 years, divided into two groups of 45 participants each. The experimental group used the intelligent interactive learning environment, while the control group received traditional oral instruction, both engaging in language learning activities for a duration of two months. The experimental results demonstrate that compared to the control group, the experimental group using the intelligent interactive learning environment exhibited higher levels of learning engagement and internal motivation.

articleTitle: A study on students’ interactive characteristics in online-personalized tutorship
abstract: Online question-and-answering (Q&A) is very important for students during online learning. Study on the interactive characteristics of online Q&A dialogues can provide useful references for teachers to design high-quality online Q&A strategies. In this study, for 31420 online Q&A dialogue records from an intelligent tutoring system, clustering was conducted based on three dimensions of dialogue frequency, duration, and content, and by defining and calculating the sentence entropy to measure discourses quality. Online Q&A dialogue presents three different types of interaction categories: low, moderate and high, and the higher interaction category corresponds to the poorer students’ knowledge level. The different categories of interactions reflect three states of Q&A dialogue sequences, namely, “little instruction, well understanding”, “precise instruction”, and “active discussion”. Teacher’s discourse quality in the first Q&A activity of students can significantly affect their subsequent interaction states. Those findings can be useful for teachers to design high-quality Q&A strategies.

articleTitle: How Connectivism is Applied to Corporate Training - Practice from China Construction Bank
abstract: Connectivism is a learning theory for the increasingly open and complex digital age. Although corporate training should be an important field of practice of this theory, there is a lack of systematic cases. China Construction Bank has carried out an innovative practice based on connectivism, considering the future development of corporate training and the need to support achieving strategic goals. This paper systematically traces this process and answers the question “how connectivism is applied to corporate training” based on a case study. The process, results and business values of the program are systematically presented to provide references for related practices.

articleTitle: Let’s Chat: Integrating Large Language Models into Blended Learning of English for Specific Purposes
abstract: English for Specific Purposes (ESP) pedagogy addresses the specific needs of language learners in professional or academic contexts by enhancing their motivation, autonomy and contextual communication skills. Despite recent fruitful approaches to blended ESP pedagogy, challenges such as learner diversity, limited classroom time and teacher resources can make real-world implementation of blended ESP learning costly and challenging. To address these issues, we propose to integrate Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT into blended ESP learning to provide personalized learning experiences through a flexible, interactive and engaging interface. We present, as an exploratory prototype, a web-based system that uses the ChatGPT API to support the administration and delivery of customizable blended ESP courses. We discuss the design, implementation and envisioned use cases of the system in a blended learning environment.

articleTitle: Do government-led online after-school tutoring program help improve students’ non-cognitive abilities? – A comparative analysis with extracurricular commercial tutoring
abstract: In order to meet students’ increasingly personalized learning needs, the Chinese government has begun to try to carry out online after-school tutoring program. This study used the Propensity Score Matching (PSM) to analyze whether government-led online after-school tutoring program help students to improve their non-cognitive abilities, and further analyzed the factors influencing students’ choice of different forms of tutoring and the difference in the effect of students’ participation in different forms of tutoring. A questionnaire survey was conducted on 1833 7th-8th grade students in China. The results showed that disadvantaged students are more likely to participate in government-led online after-school tutoring program, and such program can effectively promote students’ non-cognitive abilities, while extracurricular commercial tutoring has a negative impact on students’ learning emotion. These findings can provide new ideas and suggestions on promoting the high-quality and balanced development of education.

articleTitle: CanChat: A Cantonese Empathetic Chatbot for Secondary School Student Counseling
abstract: This study introduces an innovative Cantonese chatbot, CanChat, which is designed to enhance secondary counseling services in Hong Kong. CanChat aims to offer personalized conversations and supports to students grappling with academic and familial challenges. By engaging with students before direct interaction with school counselors, the chatbot streamlines the counseling process, enabling counselors to allocate more time to critical issues. Furthermore, CanChat supplies mental health-related information and guidance, empowering students to regulate their emotions effectively. Its integrated alert system also facilitates timely intervention by social workers when necessary. By addressing the emotional well-being of students, particularly in light of the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, CanChat seeks to create an accessible and stigma-free support system for Hong Kong’s youth. By offering assistance beyond traditional face-to-face counseling methods, this paper is expected to aspire and foster a renewed sense of confidence and comfort in discussing mental health initiatives for teenagers in Hong Kong.

articleTitle: A Mobile Driving Simulator to Improve Driving Experience for Novice and Learner Drivers
abstract: Statistics show that novice and learner drivers have a higher crash risk and lower passing rate for driving tests compared to experienced drivers, posing a risk to road safety. Therefore, we propose a mobile driving simulator game that is designed to provide an alternative driver training solution for novice and learner drivers to improve their driving experiences and prepare for the driving test. This game focuses on promoting safe driving by providing a driver training platform through smartphones, with high portability and functionality. The game consists of three modes - Tutorial, Free Driving, and Driving Test Mode. The Tutorial Mode offers driver training tutorials to teach and remind drivers of their driving knowledge. The Free Driving Mode provides an authentic Hong Kong street view to enhance drivers’ recognition of roads in Hong Kong. The Driving Test Mode offers a simulated driving test for learner drivers to practice for their driving test. The game features a high-quality and authentic map of Hong Kong, with street views, buildings, and road objects built according to real-life situations in Ho Man Tin. Players can explore the detailed map while practicing driving with the game.

articleTitle: Factors affecting Middle School Students’ Online Learning: A Study Based on the CIPP Model
abstract: While the effects of online learning on middle school students has aroused widespread attention, few studies to date have investigated factors that influence their learning outcomes and satisfaction. The present study used the Context-Input-Process-Product (CIPP) model to construct a model to understand how various aspects of online education affect online learning effects. These factors’ influencing mechanisms were analyzed using the structural equation model. The findings are as follows: 1) middle school students’ online learning presence and online learning engagement had significant positive impacts on their online learning effects, 2) their online learning engagement had a masking effect on the relationship between information literacy and online learning effects, and played a mediating role in the relationship between online learning presence and online learning effects, and 3) students’ self-regulation strategy and online learning engagement played chain mediating roles in the relationship between their online learning presence and the online learning effects.

articleTitle: Does the Blue Hat Work? The Impact of Using Six-thinking Hats in Online Collective Reflection on Pre-service Teachers Team Cohesion, Critical Thinking, and Creativity
abstract: Collective reflection refers to the process by which members of a community reflect through social interaction, as well as to the outcomes of this process. In the field of teacher education, research has shown that collaborative reflection enables teachers to engage in deeper reflection and gain the means to improve their teaching. But it also leads to problems, such as confusion and inefficiency. De Bono’s six-thinking hats refers to a parallel thinking strategy in which six coloured hats represent six different ways of thinking. It is designed to give group members a means to think together more effectively and collaboratively. The blue hat has overall planning and control function, which can make thinking more orderly and logical. The six-thinking hats have been used widely in business, medical care, and other fields but rarely for education. To explore the role of the blue hat, this study applied six-thinking hats as the thinking strategy tool in the collective reflection of pre-service teachers. This study used a quasi-experimental research method in which the control group used the six-thinking hats freely. The experimental group focused on the coordinating role of the blue hat, in the order of blue-green-blue-red-yellow-black-red-blue, etc. The study shows that focusing on using blue hat significantly increased pre-service teachers’ creativity and team cohesion and had insignificant effects on critical thinking during collective reflection by pre-service teachers.
